problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=20t-12{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=8\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (20t-12{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =10{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=8.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =10(1)^{2}-4(1)^{3}+C \\ 8 & =6+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=10{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3}+2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =10(2)^{2}-4(2)^{3}+2 \\  & =40-32+2 \\  & =10\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|$, we conclude that the speed of the particle is $10\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.$
